title: Ordered Toolcall Reconciliation & Disconnect Splay for Streaming Resilience (OpenAI compat)
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds ordered reconciliation for tool/function calls during stream reconnects and introduces a randomized disconnect splay to reduce reconnect storms. OpenAI compatibility layer now preserves toolcall ordering and surfaces deterministic idempotency tokens. Behavior is opt-in via streaming.reconnect.ordered_toolcalls config; rollout staged behind a feature flag.
description: Motivation: customers running multi-tool conversations saw non-deterministic toolcall ordering after client disconnect + rapid reconnects which caused out-of-order side effects in third-party systems. This PR introduces server-side ordering guarantees for tool/function calls across reconnect/resume boundaries plus a client disconnect splay (randomized small backoff applied server-side to accept/reconcile reconnects) to avoid thundering reconnections. Design: 1) Sequence numbers: each stream session assigns a monotonic sequence number to each emitted event that can invoke a tool. Sequence numbers are signed by the server lease and attached to events sent to the client. 2) Reconciliation window: on reconnect the client can provide latest-acked-seq; server replays pending events in-order and drops duplicates. 3) Idempotency + ordered-apply: tool call invocations include an ordered_id composed of session_id:seq so downstream adapters (and the OpenAI compat shim) can apply tools in sequence. 4) Disconnect splay: when many clients disconnect during scale events we introduce a small randomized acceptance delay (0-300ms configurable) before reattaching the session lease to avoid simultaneous inflight reconnections overwhelming the tool adapters. 5) Config and compatibility: the OpenAI compatibility layer now accepts and emits ordered_toolcalls metadata on streaming endpoints and falls back to previous behavior when the flag is off. 6) Safety: added checks so that a resumed stream with an older lease is rejected; client must re-negotiate if server lease id mismatches. Rollout plan: feature gated behind streaming.reconnect.ordered_toolcalls, enabled for canary customers for 48 hours, metric-driven rollouts tied to toolcall error-rate and tail-latency. Tests: unit tests for seq assignment and validation, integration tests simulating N concurrent reconnects with artificial clock skew, e2e tests validating toolcall ordering against a mock adapter. Docs: docs/streaming/reconnect.md updated with semantics and migration steps. Implementation notes: implementation touches the session manager, ack manager, and OpenAI adapter layers to wire ordered ids into structured output. Commits are small and focused to ease bisecting. Backwards compatibility: when the client does not provide ordered metadata we maintain existing behavior; SDKs are updated to opt into the new behavior. Observability: added metrics streaming.reconnect.splay_applied and streaming.reconcile.ordered_replays to monitor adoption.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice focused change. Can we ensure the sequence number fits in 64 bits across long-lived sessions? Also request an extra unit test for seq wrap-around detection.
Maya Patel (author): Seq is u64 currently; added a test for wrap-around detection and defensive error path that forces session renewal when seq would overflow.
Ravi Singh: The disconnect splay param seems low for high fan-out events. Suggest making the upper bound configurable per deployment and exposing metric when splay is applied.
Maya Patel (author): Made upper bound configurable via streaming.reconnect.splay_max_ms and added streaming.reconnect.splay_applied metric and dashboards in observability pack.
Priya Nair: Integration test flaked in the first run due to timing; can we add a deterministic clock or retries to stabilize? Also ensure SDK changes have clear migration notes.
Maya Patel (author): Switched integration harness to use fake clock for deterministic behavior and added migration note in docs/streaming/reconnect.md. Marking as ready-for-merge after CI green.
ci_checks: e2e: flaky on first run, rerun passed
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-02-24 by Maya Patel after approvals from reviewers. Feature gated; no immediate global rollout. Canary enabled for 3% of streaming traffic and monitored for 48 hours.
notes: Behavior is opt-in via streaming.reconnect.ordered_toolcalls; default remains backwards compatible.
SDKs: python/ts updated to include helpers for reconstructing ordered toolcall ids; patch released in minor versions.
Observability: new metrics added; dashboards updated in observability-pack repo.
Operational: when enabling globally, consider raising tool-adapter concurrency limits for first 24 hours to absorb ordered replays.
